climate_pressure: Erratic rainfall, drought periods and flooding.
documented_impact: Reported reductions/disruptions in pasture, livestock water, crops and fishing/farming livelihoods.
fcv_mediator: Competition over water, channels, grazing areas and crops, interacting with local resource-sharing rules.
possible_consequence: Under adverse governance and security conditions, these pressures may contribute to intercommunal clashes and displacement.
uncertainty: Interview-based evidence cannot estimate the climate contribution to violence.
compact_statement: Climate-related livelihood stress may aggravate already-governed resource disputes; it is not demonstrated as a sufficient cause of violence. (Refugees International)

climate_pressure: Climate shocks affect already vulnerable livelihood systems.
documented_impact: Acute food insecurity and constrained household coping.
fcv_mediator: Conflict displacement, loss/restriction of land and livelihood access, concentration of needs.
possible_consequence: Displaced and host households may become less able to absorb subsequent climate or price shocks.
geographies: Far North and other crisis regions
uncertainty: No reviewed study decomposes the relative climate/conflict contributions.
resilience_factors: accessible markets and conflict-sensitive resource access
compact_statement: Climate shocks occur inside a conflict-displacement system that can weaken coping, rather than independently producing acute hunger. (UNHCR Data Portal)

documented_impact: Poorer pasture and longer livestock movements.
fcv_mediator: Crop/grazing encroachment, livestock density, crop damage and land-tenure pressures.
possible_consequence: These interacting pressures may aggravate farmer-pastoralist conflict.
compact_statement: In Kilum-Ijim, climate variability interacts with herd pressure and land governance rather than operating as a stand-alone conflict driver. (Frontiers)

climate_pressure: Urban flood and other hazard exposure.
documented_impact: Need for resilient urban infrastructure and services.
fcv_mediator: Security problems restricted implementation and caused reductions in project scope.
possible_consequence: Conflict may leave some exposed urban communities with delayed or incomplete resilience investments.
geographies: Particularly Far North and NW/SW project locations
alternative_explanations: counterpart funding and staffing also constrained implementation
uncertainty: Project experience cannot be generalized to every municipality.
resilience_factors: municipal capacity support and conflict-sensitive delivery
compact_statement: Recent project evidence directly shows insecurity delaying or narrowing resilience investment. (World Bank)

fcv_mediator: Institutional fragmentation, limited decentralization capacity, fiscal constraints and weak data systems.
possible_consequence: Adaptation may be slower, less spatially targeted or less sustainable.
affected_groups: Especially populations dependent on weak local service systems
sectors: Cross-sectoral climate policy and public services
systems_assets_resources: Cross-sectoral climate policy and public services
alternative_explanations: normal administrative complexity and project design
uncertainty: No reviewed nationwide study estimates adaptation losses attributable to governance fragmentation.
compact_statement: Cameroon has an increasingly articulated climate architecture, but implementation bottlenecks may weaken conversion of policy into local resilience. (UNFCCC)

climate_pressure: Climate shocks are one contributor to humanitarian needs.
documented_impact: Severe food insecurity in conflict-affected regions.
fcv_mediator: Displacement and insecurity elevate needs while donor shortages reduce delivery.
possible_consequence: Reduced aid coverage could increase harmful coping or deepen vulnerability to subsequent shocks.
uncertainty: Downstream conflict/stability effects have not been evaluated.
resilience_factors: Reliable multi-year humanitarian finance and livelihood-support transitions
compact_statement: Assistance capacity is itself a mediator of whether multi-causal shocks become deeper household crises. (World Food Programme)

climate_pressure: Natural-resource stress may intensify livelihood-management challenges.
documented_impact: Water/pasture access can be a focus of community disputes.
fcv_mediator: Quality of dialogue, dispute management and inclusive resource rules.
possible_consequence: Stronger local institutions may reduce escalation even under resource stress.
alternative_explanations: Wider security trends and other interventions may explain perceived conflict reductions
uncertainty: No independent counterfactual evaluation of peace outcomes.
compact_statement: Evidence suggests local resource institutions can be peace-supporting, but the measured magnitude of their effect remains uncertain. (MPTF Gateway)

climate_pressure: Participant households face climate and non-climate shocks.
documented_impact: AEP-Youth improved measured food security but did not improve measured shock-recovery ability.
fcv_mediator: Conflict/insecurity was explicitly included among non-climate shocks in the evaluation framework.
possible_consequence: Economic or food-security improvements should not automatically be interpreted as climate/FCV resilience.
alternative_explanations: Differential shock exposure among participants and comparison households
uncertainty: Programme geography excludes major Far North and East crisis contexts.
resilience_factors: Targeted programming that explicitly measures recovery
compact_statement: Measurable livelihood gains did not automatically produce measurable shock resilience. (IFAD) ---
